findings.where: frame 140, the 'hold' object at its largest, roughly x330-580 y755-1030; the same object appears small in 01_pulse.png at x750-960 y1150-1420
findings.what: The feeling object is an untextured low-poly render: a 64x64 patch of its top face carries 1.67 per cent of its spectral power above 35 per cent of Nyquist and 0.74 per cent above 70 per cent, against 23.65 and 6.63 per cent for the blank sheet lying directly behind it in the same frame, and a horizontal cut across that top face at y=900 runs flat at 219 for a hundred pixels, flat again at 209-212, then steps down 25 and 14 grey levels to 153 and back up 32 and 21 - the hard-shaded facet edges of a coarse mesh - while a cut across the body at y=1010 falls 163 to 125 over 250 pixels in single-level steps, so the curved side carries no terminator at all.
findings.why: The row asks for feelings as physical objects; this object has a tenth of the fine surface detail of the paper it is lying on and visible polygon faceting, so it reads as an untextured clay prop rather than as a photographed thing, and it sits in the same frame as two feelings ('empty chair', 'ugh') that are ink on real paper and read correctly.

findings.where: frame 140, the shadow the 'hold' object casts on the sheet, to its right from x560 and below its base from y1030
findings.what: The object's cast shadow is a blurred silhouette of uniform density, not a contact shadow. Reading the 60th-percentile luma outward from the object (paper is 228): to the right it is 127, 128, 129, 130, 130 across x=560 to 660, then ramps 170, 227, 229 over the next 40px; below the base it is 134, 124, 125, 128, 129 then 191, 229. The shadow varies by ten levels across a hundred pixels of a hundred-level shadow, and it is at its lightest (134, 127) exactly at the contact, where a baked shadow is darkest.
findings.why: The row names this failure mode in as many words - 'contact shadows baked from the render's own lighting rather than applied as a uniform blur' - and the paper sheets in 02_chat.png do it correctly in the same build (45 to 75 levels deep at 2 to 8 px from the edge, under 9 by 16 px), so two shadow models are running side by side.

findings.what: This object is ringed by a hard, opaque, near-black outline that has no light direction. In a 25px ring around its silhouette the fraction of pixels below luma 45 is 11.6 per cent on the left, 10.5 on the right, 7.9 above and 9.6 below - equal on all four sides. A horizontal cut at y=1272 runs desk 84, then 26, 26, 29, 28, 29, 31, then 75 and up to the card at 211: a two-pixel edge into a core 64 levels below the open desk, and the core varies by two grey levels where the open desk in that same row varies from 72 to 100, so the wood grain is extinguished rather than darkened.
findings.why: Every paper sheet in the same still throws a directional contact shadow (in 01_pulse the sheets measure below-minus-above of +8 to +49 and right-minus-left of -1 to +32 grey levels), so on one screen the paper obeys a light from the upper left and this object obeys none; that is the row's 'contact shadows whose light directions disagree'.

findings.where: the desk, everywhere between and around the sheets - 39.5 per cent of this frame, and 73.6 per cent of 10_first_run.png
findings.what: The surface everything is photographed onto is itself drawn, not photographed. Three 64x64 desk patches (y210 x200, y210 x900, y2360 x300) carry 0.11 to 0.49 per cent of their spectral power above 35 per cent of Nyquist and 0.05 to 0.08 per cent above 70 per cent, with a laplacian-to-std ratio of 0.166 to 0.261; ten verified-blank 64x64 paper patches in the same frame carry 16.4 to 31.7 per cent and 2.9 to 6.1 per cent, at ratios of 0.78 to 1.57. Six 96x96 patches of the bare desk in 10_first_run.png give 0.23 to 0.58 per cent and 0.02 to 0.07 per cent. At 4x (x300-500, y205-285) the wood between the grain lines is featureless - no pore, no fibre, no dust, no specular - and the knot at 01_pulse x1180-1330 y1195-1330 is a set of smooth concentric ellipses.
findings.why: Material truth is a property of the whole surface, and the ground that carries every contact shadow in the build has a fiftieth of the fine detail of the paper lying on it, so at any real zoom the paper reads as a photograph pasted onto an illustration.

findings.what: Five sheets in one frame are machine-cut rectangles rather than torn paper. Fitting and removing the tilt, all four edges of each measure between 0.00 and 0.79 px rms (one exception, the left edge of the last card at 5.48), against 8.57 px rms for the most torn sheet edge in 02_chat.png; the top edge of the 'TO DO' card holds y=737 or 738 for its whole 700-column width after a corner that rounds over about six pixels. Their surface tooth is genuine (20 to 38 per cent of power above 35 per cent of Nyquist, the same as the torn entry sheets below them), so this is real scanned stock cut with a blade, not a fill.
findings.why: It does not trip the anti-goal, because the surface is photographed paper rather than a beige stand-in, but a rounded rectangle with a soft shadow is exactly the shape the concept is defined against, and it changes the material register halfway down a single screen.

findings.where: the top edges of the voice-note sheet at y675-899, the sheet at y926-1232 and the sheet at y2131-2355
findings.what: Three of the eight sheets on the glass have a machine-straight top edge. Sub-pixel traces of the fourteen top and bottom edges give tear amplitudes from 0.30 px rms (the voice note: 3.5 px peak to peak over 961 columns) and 0.56 and 0.85 px, up to 8.57 px rms and 49.7 px peak to peak for the sheet at y1285-1667. At x500 to 600 the voice note's desk-to-paper transition sits on rows 676-679 in every single column - 104, 158, 219, 229 - so the edge does not move by one pixel across a hundred.
findings.why: One cut edge on a torn sheet is honest, but three sheets of eight carrying a ruled top while their neighbours carry fibrous 50-pixel tears means the paper in one frame was not all made the same way.

findings.where: absent from the set, together with 16_setup_android.png
findings.what: The two Android artifacts are missing. MANIFEST.json and WHY_MISSING.json give a measured reason rather than an assertion - no /dev/kvm, so the x86_64 image runs under QEMU instruction emulation, adbd answered after 113 minutes and the framework never came up behind it, there is no GTK for a desktop stand-in, and nothing was faked from the PWA.
findings.why: That is a reason and not an excuse, and nothing was substituted, but it does mean no surface in this build has ever been judged on the Android screen the mission names, and a paper texture is exactly the thing a different renderer and a different panel can break.

findings.where: the whole grid, and the same in 14_media_viewer.png
findings.what: The one place in the build where an actual photograph would appear holds CG renders instead: untextured grey rooms, a black sphere on a plane, a bare table, and in 14_media_viewer a synthetic water surface with scattered blue marks.
findings.why: Adjacent to this row rather than inside it, but it is the only place a real photograph could sit in a build whose whole claim is photographed material, and there is not one.

what_is_working: The paper is a real scan and measurably not procedural. High-passed blank paper on three sheets of 02_chat.png has kurtosis of +5.5, +8.8 and +12.6 and skew of -1.5, -1.6 and -1.8 - heavy-tailed and asymmetric, the signature of fibre and speck - where synthetic white noise and synthetic band-limited noise controls give kurtosis 0.03 and 0.00 and skew 0.00 and 0.02. Directional anisotropy is 2.5 to 4.7 with a preferred fibre direction that differs between sheets (0, 0 and 90 degrees), so it is not one noise field laid over everything.

No tear repeats within the Chat hero. Fourteen edges traced sub-pixel from the seven whole sheets, median-filtered and high-passed above about 120 px, compared over all 91 pairs with a search across plus or minus 250 px of shift and a mirror: the best match is r = 0.584 between two edges whose amplitudes differ by a factor of four, and not one pair reaches r > 0.85 with amplitudes within 20 per cent. The five tab pieces at the foot of the frame, rectified and with the light-to-dark step removed, match each other at no better than r = 0.384.

Sharing a paper stock does not produce a visible repeat. The capture record puts lined_01 on three of the eight sheets and legal_01 on two; with every rule and every mark of ink masked out, the fibre of the same-stock pairs correlates at 0.36 to 0.50 and the different-stock pairs at 0.18 to 0.45 - indistinguishable - against a ceiling of 1.00 for a patch against itself. The crop offset into the scan is randomised, so a reused stock does not read as a reused sheet.

The desk is not a tile. Correlating the desk against itself over 1196 vertical offsets gives a monotone decay from 0.86 at four pixels to a median of 0.024, with no revival at any offset; horizontally the best match beyond 40 px is 0.33 at 145 px, which is grain spacing, not a seam.

The paper's contact shadows all agree on one light and are baked per sheet. All seven thread sheets in 02_chat.png are darker below than above (by +6.4 to +67.3 grey levels) and darker right than left (by +7.0 to +62.7): seven of seven, light from the upper left. They are not one blur: the darkening above is a near-constant 7 to 15 levels of occlusion while the darkening below peaks at 22 to 75 and is back under 9 by 16 px, and the reach differs sheet by sheet - the voice note peaks at 2 px and is spent by 8, while the sheet at y1285-1667 peaks at 16 - so each sheet sits at its own height above the desk.

The handwriting carries real variants and real pressure. Of 391 normalised ink marks across the six handwritten sheets (the voice-note waveform excluded, since its bars are identical by design), 14,726 pairs are close enough in size to be the same glyph; only 38 of them (0.26 per cent) reach IoU 0.9 and 9 (0.06 per cent) reach 0.95, with a median of 0.284. Stroke width measured off the rendered pixels varies with a coefficient of 0.151 to 0.290 per hand and ink depth with 0.189 to 0.394, and the two hands differ from each other (mean stroke 4.06 px against 4.49).

The fold in 06_unfolding.mp4 is rendered geometry catching light, not a flat image being transformed. The tilted panel's value tracks its angle to the light - a mean of 180 at frame 49, 205 at 65, 223 at 73 and 237 when flat - and the bend itself carries a self-shadow trough: at frame 73 the panel rises 214 to 223 and then falls back to 213 over four rows just before the crease, and at frame 85 it rises to 237 and falls to 215 over five rows, and only then does the far panel resume at 234. A flat sheet swung on a hinge has no such valley. At full resolution the folding sheet also carries fibrous torn edges and paper tooth, which the six-frame strip is too small to show.
verdict: The thing this row exists to test - whether the paper reads as photographed - is true, and true on measurement rather than on impression. At three hundred per cent the Chat hero holds real scanned stock (kurtosis +5.5 to +12.6 and skew -1.5 to -1.8 against Gaussian controls at zero), eight tears that do not repeat across all 91 pairwise comparisons, handwriting whose repeated glyphs reach identity 0.06 per cent of the time, and seven contact shadows that agree on one light from the upper left and differ from each other in reach, which is what baked shadows do and what a uniform blur cannot. In slow motion the fold is geometry, not a transform: the panel's value tracks its angle and the crease carries a self-shadow trough of about twenty grey levels over five rows. None of the three materials that would force this category below its floor - a procedural noise overlay, a tiled repeating texture, a beige rounded rectangle standing in for paper - is present; I tested for each and each is measurably absent. What is short is everything that is not paper. The desk that carries every one of those shadows is a drawing: a fiftieth of the paper's fine detail, a knot made of smooth concentric ellipses, and it is 39.5 per cent of the Chat hero and 73.6 per cent of the first-run screen. Four of the six feelings in the Pulse row are untextured low-poly renders whose largest presentation shows countable facets and a tenth of the paper's tooth; one of them casts a shadow of uniform density that is lightest at the contact, which is the failure this row names by name, and another is ringed by an opaque near-black outline with no light direction at all, on the same screen as sheets that obey one. Four of the row's six clauses are met cleanly and the two named viewing tests both pass; two clauses have specific measured failures on the feeling objects, and the ground under everything is drawn. Twenty-one of twenty-five, one under the floor: the paper is genuinely photographed, and almost nothing else in the frame is.

not_worth_opening.path: evidence/08_state_propagating.mp4 and evidence/15_authored_feeling.mp4 and evidence/11_chat_scroll.mp4 (the video files themselves)
not_worth_opening.reason: I stepped through their six-frame strips in evidence/crops/ and they show the same paper, the same desk and the same feeling objects I had already measured frame by frame in 06_unfolding.mp4 and 07_feeling_landing.mp4. My row is judged on the Chat hero and the unfolding clip, and extracting three more clips would have repeated measurements I had already taken rather than adding a surface.
Per-frame scroll physics and WebKit build-and-raster cost. Neither says anything about whether a surface is photographed; they belong to a motion or performance row.
23 KB of vibration waveforms. I opened haptics.check.json and the strip to see what they are; the waveforms themselves have no material surface.
Sync faults, load timings and the app's copy. Read for a messenger-completeness row and a voice row; none of them can make a tear repeat or a shadow disagree.

not_worth_opening.path: evidence/crops/reception_allowed.png, reception_open.png, reception_replaced.png and evidence/logs/reception*.json beyond the first
not_worth_opening.reason: The record says in as many words that these are Chromium on a Linux virtual display, not an artifact and not an iPhone. I opened reception.json and reception.png to confirm what they are; the rest is notification delivery, not material.

not_worth_opening.path: the per-scene logs for 01, 03, 04, 05, 10, 12, 13, 14, 17 and dusk_pulse
not_worth_opening.reason: I opened those ten stills themselves and measured on the pixels. The scene logs record what the app believed it was showing (message ids, delivery states, scroll positions), which is a completeness question; where a log made a material claim I could check - the eight tear names and eight stock names in 02_chat.report.json - I opened it and checked it against the file.
